title: Global View - Immigration and Customs

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
My name is Marco.
My name is Catherine.
And today we're doing something that makes a lot of people very nervous when they come to America.
segments.zh: 今天我们正在做一些让很多人来到美国时非常紧张的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
Today we are arriving to the airport, but before we can leave, we need to pass through customs and immigration.
segments.zh: 今天我们到达机场，但在我们离开之前，我们需要通过海关和移民局。

segments.en: All right.
Customs and immigration.
So anyone who comes into the United States, American, not American, doesn't matter, you have to go through this gate.
segments.zh: 所以任何进入美国的人，美国人，而不是美国人，都无关紧要，你必须通过这个大门。

segments.en: So let's learn about some of these phrases and questions in today's dialogue.
segments.zh: 因此，让我们在今天的对话中了解其中的一些短语和问题。

segments.en: Good afternoon.
Passport and arrival card, please.
Here you are.
Where are you coming from?
China.
Is this your country of birth or residence?
segments.zh: 这是您的出生国还是居住国？

segments.en: I just worked there.
What is the purpose of your visit to the United States?
segments.zh: 您访问美国的目的是什么？

segments.en: I'm here on vacation.
How long do you plan to stay in the United States?
Almost three weeks.
Sir, you didn't fill out the information on your arrival card of where you'll be staying.
segments.zh: 先生，您的入境卡上没填在美国的住址。

segments.en: Oh, I'm sorry, but there are a couple of different places I will travel to within the United States, so I wasn't sure what to put.
segments.zh: 抱歉，我会去美国好几个地方旅行，所以不确定该填哪里。

segments.en: You must specify an address on the place where you will spend most of your time.
segments.zh: 您必须填写停留时间最长的地方的地址。

segments.en: Okay.
Here you are.
Do you have enough means to support yourself while you're here?
segments.zh: 您在这里期间有足够的资金维持生活吗？

segments.en: Yes, I have some travelers checks and two credit cards.
segments.zh: 有，我带了旅行支票和两张信用卡。

segments.en: Very good.
Do you have anything to declare?
Nope.
I only have my clothes and camera.
segments.zh: 我只有我的衣服和相机。

segments.en: Very well, sir.
Welcome to the United States.
Enjoy your visit.
All right, we're back.
So now let's take a look at some of that language takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们来看看一些语言的收获。

segments.en: Language takeaway.
The first thing we have to learn about is the arrival card.
segments.zh: 我们首先要了解的是到达卡。

segments.en: So good afternoon, passport and arrival card, please.
segments.zh: 下午好，护照和到达卡，拜托。

segments.en: That's the first line of the dialogue.
That's right.

So the arrival card, usually you will get on the airplane before you land, and basically you just have to put your name, your passport number, where you're from, and basic information like this that you must give to the immigration officer.
segments.zh: 所以到达卡，通常你会在降落前上飞机，基本上你只需要输入你的名字、你的护照号码、你来自哪里，以及你必须提供给移民官的基本信息。

segments.en: Great.
So what is the opposite of arrival card?
segments.zh: 那么抵达卡的反义词是什么？

segments.en: What do you fill out when you leave America?
segments.zh: 当你离开美国时，你会填写什么？

segments.en: That's right.
Some countries require you to fill out a departure card.
segments.zh: 有些国家要求您填写出发卡。

segments.en: All right.
So some countries, not all, but you'll usually get an arrival card, which means that you have to give your name and basic information.
segments.zh: 所以有些国家，不是全部，但你通常会得到一张到达卡，这意味着你必须提供你的名字和基本信息。

segments.en: That's right.
So we are talking to the immigration officer, and he asks, is this your country of birth or residence?
segments.zh: 所以我们正在与移民官交谈，他问，这是你的出生国还是居住国？

segments.en: All right, let's break that down.
Country of birth.
So birth, birthday, that makes me think of where I was born.
segments.zh: 所以出生，生日，这让我想起了我出生的地方。

segments.en: So what country were you born in?
That's another way to ask this question.
segments.zh: 这是问这个问题的另一种方式。

segments.en: That's right.
So since we said we are coming from China, the immigration officer wants to know if we are Chinese or if we simply live there, and that's why he says or residence.
segments.zh: 所以既然我们说我们来自中国，移民官想知道我们是中国人还是我们只是住在那里，这就是他说或居住的原因。

segments.en: So residence, it's a noun, it's a thing.
segments.zh: 所以居住，它是一个名词，它是一个东西。

segments.en: My country of residence is the place where I live.
segments.zh: 我的居住国是我住的地方。

segments.en: So I'm American, but maybe my country of residence is France because I live in France.
segments.zh: 所以我是美国人，但也许我的居住国是法国，因为我住在法国。

segments.en: That's right.
So it's different from your country of birth.
segments.zh: 所以它与你的出生国不同。

segments.en: Now moving on, when the immigration officer was asking us about money, we said that we have some traveler's checks and two credit cards.
segments.zh: 现在继续前进，当移民官向我们询问金钱时，我们说我们有一些旅行支票和两张信用卡。

segments.en: All right, so credit cards are pretty clear, but what exactly are traveler's checks and how are they different from normal checks?
segments.zh: 好吧，信用卡很清楚，但是旅行支票到底是什么，它们与普通支票有何不同？

segments.en: So traveler's checks are kind of a convenient way to carry money because you have these little pieces of paper that have a certain amount on them.
segments.zh: 所以旅行支票是一种方便的携带钱的方式，因为你有这些小纸片，上面有一定的数量。

segments.en: So for example, $500 each, and if you lose it, it's not a problem because no one can exchange those checks for cash unless it's you.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，每个 500 美元，如果您丢失它，这不是问题，因为除非是您，否则没有人可以将这些支票兑换成现金。

segments.en: All right, so my traveler's check, I buy these from the bank.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我的旅行支票，我从银行买了这些。

segments.en: They have my name on them, my passport number on them, and to spend them as money, I need to show my passport or proof of identification or proof of identity.
segments.zh: 他们有我的名字，上面有我的护照号码，为了把它们作为钱花，我需要出示我的护照或身份证明或身份证明。

segments.en: So basically, if someone steals my traveler's checks, if I lose my traveler's checks, I don't have to worry because no one else can spend them but me.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，如果有人偷了我的旅行支票，如果我丢失了旅行者的支票，我不必担心，因为除了我之外没有其他人可以花掉它们。

segments.en: Exactly.
They were very, very popular back before credit cards were so popular.
segments.zh: 在信用卡如此受欢迎之前，它们非常非常受欢迎。

segments.en: Now you don't really see too many traveler's checks, but it's still convenient.
segments.zh: 现在你并没有真正看到太多的旅行支票，但它仍然很方便。

segments.en: All right, so a lot of language there.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以那里有很多语言。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to our dialogue again?
segments.zh: 为什么我们不再听我们的对话？

segments.en: Good afternoon.
Passport and arrival card, please.
Here you are.
Where are you coming from?
China.
Is this your country of birth or residence?
segments.zh: 这是您的出生国还是居住国？

segments.en: I just worked there.
What is the purpose of your visit to the United States?
segments.zh: 您访问美国的目的是什么？

segments.en: I'm here on vacation.

Almost three weeks.
Sir, you didn't fill out the information on your arrival card of where you'll be staying.
segments.zh: 先生，您的入境卡上没填在美国的住址。

segments.en: Oh, I'm sorry, but there are a couple of different places I will travel to within the United States, so I wasn't sure what to put.

segments.en: You must specify an address on the place where you will spend most of your time.
segments.zh: 您必须填写停留时间最长的地方的地址。

segments.en: Okay.
Here you are.
Do you have enough means to support yourself while you're here?
segments.zh: 您在这里期间有足够的资金维持生活吗？

segments.en: Yes, I have some traveler's checks and two credit cards.
segments.zh: 是的，我有一些旅行支票和两张信用卡。

segments.en: Very good.

Nope.

segments.zh: 我只有我的衣服和相机。

segments.en: Very well, sir.

Enjoy your visit.
All right, we're back.
So now let's take a look at some of those key questions that the immigration officer asks us on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们来看看移民官在流利建设者中问我们的一些关键问题。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
All right, this first sentence, this first question is actually something that a lot of learners of English have a hard time with.
segments.zh: 好吧，这第一句话，第一个问题实际上是很多英语学习者很难接受的。

segments.en: Where are you coming from?
Right.
So the immigration officer is sitting there at his desk and you are arriving on an airplane.
segments.zh: 所以移民官坐在他的办公桌前，你要坐飞机。

segments.en: So what he wants to know is what country are you arriving from?
segments.zh: 那么他想知道的是你来自哪个国家？

segments.en: So if I am on a flight from France to America, I say I'm arriving from France.
segments.zh: 因此，如果我乘坐从法国飞往美国的航班，我会说我要从法国抵达。

segments.en: I'm coming from France.
That's right.
But here's a big thing.
What if he says, where are you from?
Now he's asking you for your nationality.
So then you wouldn't say France because you're not French.
segments.zh: 所以你不会说法国，因为你不是法国人。

segments.en: I'm not French.
I'm American.
So I'd say I am American, but I'm coming from France.
segments.zh: 所以我会说我是美国人，但我来自法国。

segments.en: So this is a very typical question that English learners confuse because as you can see, it's very, very similar, but you just have one word that you add on and it completely changes the question.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常典型的问题，英语学习者会混淆，因为正如你所看到的，它非常非常相似，但你只有一个词，你添加了一个词，它完全改变了问题。

segments.en: So when the immigration officer asks you, where are you coming from?
segments.zh: 所以当移民官问你时，你来自哪里？

segments.en: You tell them what country you got on the plane.
segments.zh: 你告诉他们你在飞机上的国家。

segments.en: All right.
So where did you leave to come to America?
segments.zh: 那么你去哪里来美国呢？

segments.en: Did you leave from France, China, Ghana?
segments.zh: 你是从法国、中国、加纳离开的吗？

segments.en: So that's the answer to that question.
segments.zh: 所以这就是这个问题的答案。

segments.en: Exactly.
Most of the time, immigration officers will never ask you where you are from because they will see your passport.
segments.zh: 大多数时候，移民官员永远不会问你来自哪里，因为他们会看到你的护照。

segments.en: They know.
They know.
So, okay.
Now, once we give them our passport, we tell them that we just work in China.
segments.zh: 现在，一旦我们给他们护照，我们就告诉他们我们只是在中国工作。

segments.en: We're not Chinese.
He asks, what is the purpose of your visit to the United States?
segments.zh: 他问，你访问美国的目的是什么？

segments.en: What's the purpose of your visit?
Now purpose means goal or aim.
segments.zh: 现在目的意味着目标或目标。

segments.en: So there are a couple of standard answers to this question, but basically the immigration officer wants to know, why are you in America?
segments.zh: 所以这个问题有几个标准的答案，但基本上移民官想知道，你为什么在美国？

segments.en: Why are you coming here?
That's right.
So you have, as Catherine says, a couple of different ways of answering that.
segments.zh: 所以，正如凯瑟琳所说，你有几种不同的方式来回答这个问题。

segments.en: We're saying here that we are here on vacation.
segments.zh: 我们在这里说我们在这里度假。

segments.en: I'm here on vacation.
Tourism.
Tourism.
Business.
Right.
Seeing family.
These are all acceptable answers.
segments.zh: 这些都是可接受的答案。

segments.en: That's right.
So now that we've told the officer all of this information, we actually forgot to fill out our address on our arrival card.
segments.zh: 所以既然我们已经告诉了警官所有这些信息，我们实际上忘记在我们的到达卡上填写我们的地址。

segments.en: So he says that we must specify an address.
segments.zh: 所以他说我们必须指定一个地址。

segments.en: All right.
So to specify, this is a verb.
segments.zh: 具体来说，这是一个动词。

segments.en: It means to indicate or write down or identify because right now there is no address where we're going to stay.
segments.zh: 这意味着指示或写下或识别，因为现在我们没有地址。

segments.en: So to specify means to basically to tell someone where it is, to be exact.
segments.zh: 所以指定意味着基本上告诉某人它在哪里，确切地说。

segments.en: That's right.
So you need to specify an address of where you will be during the time you're in the United States.
segments.zh: 因此，您需要指定您在美国期间的地址。

segments.en: It could be a hotel, any place.
segments.zh: 它可以是酒店，任何地方。

segments.en: Right.
But it can't be like Chicago.
segments.zh: 但它不能像芝加哥一样。

segments.en: Right.
No, it can't be a city.
segments.zh: 不，它不可能是一座城市。

segments.en: It's got to be an address.
Address.
So 10 South Street, Chicago, Illinois.
segments.zh: 所以 10 South Street, Chicago, 伊利诺伊州。

segments.en: That's right.
Now we told the immigration officer where we're going to be and he asks a very important question, also very, very common.
segments.zh: 现在我们告诉移民官我们要去哪里，他问了一个非常重要的问题，也非常非常常见。

segments.en: Do you have enough means to support yourself while you are here?
segments.zh: 当你在这里时，你有足够的方式来支持自己吗？

segments.en: So means in this instance means resources or money.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下意味着资源或金钱。

segments.en: So do you have enough money to pay for your housing, your food?
segments.zh: 那么你有足够的钱来支付你的住房和食物吗？

segments.en: That's the question.
Right.
So means to support yourself.
That means can you pay for yourself?
segments.zh: 这意味着你能为自己付钱吗？

segments.en: Who's paying for this trip?
Exactly.
So this is why we say, yeah, we have some traveler's checks and a couple of credit cards.
segments.zh: 所以这就是为什么我们说，是的，我们有一些旅行支票和几张信用卡。

segments.en: And lastly, we also need to answer if we have anything to declare.
segments.zh: 最后，我们还需要回答是否有任何要声明的问题。

segments.en: But what does this mean?
To declare what?
To declare at customs.
Okay.
But we don't normally ask to declare at customs.
segments.zh: 但我们通常不要求在海关申报。

segments.en: We just say, do you have anything to declare?
segments.zh: 我们只是说，你有什么要申报的吗？

segments.en: This is because normally when we travel to other countries, there are special taxes for certain goods.
segments.zh: 这是因为通常当我们去其他国家旅行时，某些商品会有特殊税收。

segments.en: For example, if I want to come to America and I have three bottles of wine, I have to give one away because I'm only allowed to bring in two bottles.
segments.zh: 例如，如果我想来美国，我有三瓶酒，我必须赠送一瓶，因为我只能带两瓶。

segments.en: Right.
So I have to declare two bottles of wine or money.
segments.zh: 所以我必须申报两瓶酒或钱。

segments.en: I'm only allowed to bring $10,000.
If I bring $15,000, I have to write that down and say, I have this extra money and then I pay tax.
segments.zh: 如果我带了 15,000 美元，我必须把它写下来说，我有这笔额外的钱，然后我纳税。

segments.en: So basically they will ask you, what are you bringing to America?
segments.zh: 所以基本上他们会问你，你给美国带来了什么？

segments.en: And if there are special things like money or things you will sell or alcohol, cigarettes, you have to declare these.
segments.zh: 如果有一些特殊的东西，比如你要卖的东西或酒、香烟，你必须申报这些。

segments.en: You have to explain what you're carrying.
segments.zh: 你必须解释你携带的东西。

segments.en: That's right.
So this is a very important question.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常重要的问题。

segments.en: Also most of the time, obviously if you're on tourism, you don't have much to declare, but maybe like if Catherine says, maybe you are going to buy a house in the United States and you have $20,000 in your luggage, then you need to tell them that.
segments.zh: 同样大多数时候，显然如果你在旅游，你没有太多要申报的，但也许就像如果凯瑟琳说，也许你要在美国买房子，你的行李里有 20,000 美元，那么你需要告诉他们。

segments.en: That's right.
So that's called declaring, to declare at customs.
segments.zh: 所以这称为声明，在海关申报。

segments.en: All right.
So let's take a break and listen to our dialogue one last time.
segments.zh: 所以让我们休息一下，听听我们最后一次的对话。

segments.en: You will be asked.
But when you're arriving there, there are actually two different sections that you have to go to, right?
segments.zh: 但是当你到达那里时，实际上你必须去两个不同的部分，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
There's two different lines.
Maybe many lines, but they'll have a sign on top.
segments.zh: 也许很多行，但他们会在上面有一个标志。

segments.en: One says US passports or US passport holders, and that means the line for Americans coming home to America.
segments.zh: 有人说美国护照或美国护照持有人，这意味着美国人回到美国的路线。

segments.en: But for most people who are traveling to America, they're foreigners, they have to go to the other line.
segments.zh: 但对于大多数去美国旅行的人来说，他们是外国人，他们必须去另一条线。

segments.en: So that's non-US passport holders.
segments.zh: 所以这是非美国护照持有人。

segments.en: That's right.
Now remember that you don't really have to get nervous when you're talking to the immigration officer.
segments.zh: 现在请记住，当您与移民官员交谈时，您不必感到紧张。

segments.en: You have to take it easy and just try to answer the questions.
segments.zh: 你必须放轻松，只是尝试回答问题。

segments.en: Most of them will speak a couple of words in many popular languages like Chinese or Spanish or Arabic.
segments.zh: 他们中的大多数人会用许多流行语言（如中文或西班牙语或阿拉伯语）说几个词。

segments.en: Because obviously some people that go on holiday to the United States, maybe they don't speak English.
segments.zh: 因为显然有些人去美国度假，也许他们不会说英语。

segments.en: That's right.
So there's nothing to be worried about.
segments.zh: 所以没有什么好担心的。

segments.en: These people are there to make sure that America is safe.
segments.zh: 这些人在那里确保美国是安全的。

segments.en: They want to check the bags.
They want to know who's coming into the country.
segments.zh: 他们想知道谁来这个国家。

segments.en: And they're just doing their job being basically policing the borders.
segments.zh: 他们只是在做他们的工作，基本上是监管边界。

segments.en: But it's pretty simple.
The most annoying part of customs for me is waiting in line.
